newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Angry protesters swarm Albanian town centre.
newsitem.headline: Angry protesters swarm Albanian town centre.

text.p: Albanian protesters marched noisily through this southern town on Friday and skirmished with police.
The protesters threw a dozen stones at some 100 riot police who tried to push them back from the central square.

The police quickly gave ground and the situation became calmer but tense with about 5,000 protesters chanting "Down with (President Sali) Berisha" and "We want our money back" as they milled around near the town hall which was burned by a crowd last month.

Fier is about 140 km (85 miles) south of Tirana. Demonstrators in the town clashed on Thursday with a gang of men in civilian clothes, who were armed with wooden clubs and iron bars. Six people were injured, one seriously in the eye.
The local chairman of Berisha's Democratic Party, which governs the town, said local groups were being organised to protect its citizens from the protesters.

"We are organising a group of our own supporters to protect people from these illegal demonstrations," said Belul Celo. He would not say whether these were among the people who broke up Thursday's protest.
Albania has been hit by a succession of anti-government protests over the past month, fuelled by thousands of investors who lost heavily in failed high-risk investment schemes.
Investors blame the right-wing government for permitting the dubious schemes to flourish over the past five years and are demanding reimbursement by the government.
So far, the government has seized about $300 million in assets from two failed funds, which it will distribute to investors, but it says it has no intention of covering losses by the private schemes.
